entries.title: Hydrogen in Practice: A Global Review of Demonstration Projects from Production to Integration
entries.abstract: Hydrogen technology has the potential to address various challenges related to integrating low- and zero-carbon energy sources, as well as achieving carbon neutrality. It provides valuable solutions for transitioning to net-zero emission energy systems on a global scale. The implementation of hydrogen production and integration demonstration projects has received significant attention around the world and strong support from governments, highlighting the crucial role of such initiatives in the advancement of hydrogen energy. However, research in this area remains limited, particularly in terms of comprehensive and systematic reviews of industrial practices under real-world conditions. To bridge this gap, this article provides an in-depth review of hydrogen production, storage, and industrial applications, summarizing key features of thirteen exemplary hydrogen demonstration projects from around the world. The goal is to offer insights and guidance for the large-scale deployment of hydrogen energy while identifying potential technological pathways for the future.
entries.journalRef: Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews, vol. 242, 117314, 2026

entries.title: Fault Diagnosis and Fault-Tolerant Operation Strategy for Triple-Port Hydrogen Production System
entries.abstract: The multi-port converter offers significant advantages in sustainable energy-based hydrogen production, such as high energy density and wide application potential. As the core energy hub in these systems, the multi-port hydrogen converter demands high reliability. However, its numerous switches and complex operation increase the risk of failure. Currently, there are no effective fault diagnosis or fault tolerance solutions for these systems. Current fault diagnosis methods for two-port and multi-port converters rely on many sensors, have low accuracy, and cannot handle multi-switch faults. Additionally, existing fault tolerance strategies fall short in maintaining stable power for the electrolyzer and do not allow capacity sharing among ports. This paper proposes a fault diagnosis method for open-circuit faults in a triple-port hydrogen converter and a corresponding fault-tolerant operating strategy. By optimizing a random forest algorithm with a sparrow search algorithm, high-precision multi-switch fault diagnosis is achieved using only three current sensors. Fault-tolerant operation of the system is achieved through an auxiliary switch after a failure. Additionally, power sharing between output ports can be realized. This ensures the efficient and stable operation of the hydrogen production system. The effectiveness of this solution has been validated through simulations and experiments.
entries.journalRef: IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics, vol. 40, no. 8, pp. 11526-11536, 2025

entries.title: Switching Structure and Finite-Event Optima for One-Orbit Minimum-Fuel In-Plane HCW Maneuvers
entries.abstract: Under in-plane Hill–Clohessy–Wiltshire dynamics with independently bounded radial and along-track thrust, we prove that every target reachable within one orbit has a fixed-time minimum-fuel control with at most ten switches. We first show that regular optima have at most four radial and six along-track switches, coupled through a shared costate. Of the 35 candidate count pairs, 11 require minimum durations, one cannot be optimal, and 23 are attainable at arbitrarily short durations. We then convert singular-arc optima into bang/off optima with at most five switches by preserving terminal moments. We demonstrate terminal accuracy and whole-arc Pontryagin consistency through 55,296 numerical transfers.

entries.title: Optimal Coordination of Multiple Ancillary Service Provisions in Active Distribution Networks
entries.abstract: We propose a multi-rate model predictive control (MPC) framework for coordinating primary frequency control (PFC), automatic generation control (AGC), and voltage control (VC) in active distribution networks. The framework allocates distributed energy resource (DER) flexibility among these three ancillary services while retaining their different update rates. To account for the intertemporal flexibility of electric vehicle aggregations and aggregations of buildings with thermostatically controlled loads (TCLs), we incorporate time-varying power-energy envelopes into our multi-rate MPC formulation. These constraints couple the combined PFC and AGC response to the demand-side flexibility available later in the prediction horizon. Furthermore, the input-multirate structure enables coordinated ancillary service provision by DERs with different response dynamics. The controller optimizes the three services together, allowing fast regulation to be coordinated with the developing slow response within the available DER flexibility. We demonstrate the coordinated provision of the three ancillary services through closed-loop simulations on a modified IEEE 33-bus system using a nonlinear differential-algebraic model.

entries.title: Detecting Small Space Objects for Space Situational Awareness with Collaborative Edge AI
entries.abstract: With the rapid growth of space activities, near-Earth space is becoming increasingly congested, leading to a higher risk of spacecraft collisions and space debris generation. Recent close-proximity encounters and collision incidents necessitate efficient and cost-effective onboard systems for space object detection (SOD) and collision avoidance. While deep learning (DL) enabled Edge AI using low-cost vision sensors on single or multiple satellites has shown promises for SOD, significant challenges remain, including limited datasets, small SOD, and the lack of comprehensive performance assessments. This paper presents a collaborative Edge AI framework for multiview SOD and systematically benchmarks DL models and fusion strategies. Results show that higher image resolution significantly improves small SOD. For multiple views, image-level fusion reduces the combined communication and inference latency by 30.13% and 32.80% on average compared with feature-level and attention-based fusion across the evaluated inter-satellite link (ISL) bandwidth. For larger view sets, feature-level and attention-based fusion achieve better detection accuracy at the cost of analysis in the sensing-communication pipeline, revealing that multiview collaboration introduces minimal latency overhead under ISL constraints when reception capacity is not exceeded. Our work provides valuable design insights for future collaborative satellite network design, supporting the emerging space situational awareness and space traffic management requirements.

entries.title: Enforcing Ellipsoidal Constraints in Neural Networks with a Polynomial Safety Layer
entries.abstract: Often the output of a learned mapping must satisfy prescribed constraints. In the control of autonomous systems, for example, the chosen action must keep the system within a collision-free region. We consider the case in which a proposed output is corrected by projection onto a safety ellipsoid. Computing this projection amounts to solving a quadratically constrained quadratic program (QCQP). We construct a neural-network safety layer by unrolling a feasibility-preserving polynomial penalty iteration. The unrolled structure allows the loss gradient to propagate from the feasible output through the safety layer to the network parameters during training. We show how to choose the layer parameters so that every iterate is feasible and give a computable bound on its distance to the exact projection at any prescribed depth. We illustrate the method by training a LiDAR-based policy to control an unmanned aerial vehicle. A privileged model predictive control expert uses the map and the measured vehicle state to generate the training data. In the simulated narrow mazes, the filtered policy avoided wall contact at every tested stage of training, including at initialization, when every unfiltered flight hit a wall. A representative build of the learned policy and its safety layer for an Arm Cortex-M4F microcontroller occupies about 36 KiB of flash, with a RAM budget below 5 KiB.

entries.title: Gradient-Based Co-Design of Systems and Reinforcement Learning Policies with Differentiable Simulators
entries.abstract: Co-design is the problem of jointly optimizing the design of a system and the policy that operates it. Neither can be chosen independently: a system design is only as good as the policy trained for it, and the optimal policy changes with the design. When that policy is learned by reinforcement learning (RL), evaluating a candidate design requires a full policy training run, and the design is usually optimized by black-box search such as Bayesian optimization (BO) or evolution strategies (ES). These methods scale poorly with the design dimension and ignore the differentiable structure of modern simulators and, in particular, the sensitivity of the optimal policy with respect to the design. We instead derive a gradient-based co-design method, where the design gradient decomposes into a direct effect of changing the design at a fixed policy and an indirect effect through the design-dependent optimal policy. The indirect effect requires the sensitivity of the converged policy to the design, which we obtain by applying the implicit function theorem to the stationarity condition of the policy gradient. Based on this sensitivity, we develop a proof-of-concept co-design algorithm with stochastic value gradient (SVG)-style policy optimization, prove that it converges to an approximately stationary design, and demonstrate on a differentiable networked-system benchmark with high-dimensional design spaces that it consistently outperforms BO and ES.

entries.title: The Data Debt of Stockouts: Partial Identification and Minimax-Regret Inventory Control
entries.abstract: Problem definition: Inventory decisions select which demand enters sales logs. Unrecorded forecasts can leave demand frequencies unidentified even when stocking levels are recorded. We study which multistage ordering decisions these logs can justify and what finite samples can guarantee. Methodology/results: Nested stockout thresholds yield exact sets of compatible demand laws and finite representations for policy evaluation. We choose one deterministic inventory rule to minimize its largest expected cost gap from the informed optimum under the same law. This population value is data debt for the specified information and policy class. Under independent demand, carryover can create positive debt despite common optimal actions in every isolated period. Finite samples add learning error above debt. The required sample count grows linearly with the selection bound, with upper and lower orders matching up to logarithmic factors. This rate requires fixed demand and cost bounds, sufficient revelation, and a uniformly positive probability of clearing all feasible stock across the confidence sets. Controlled and semi-synthetic studies separate policy improvements from tighter guarantees. Managerial implications: More records can tighten guarantees while debt persists. Deeper revelation can establish common optimality without fully identifying demand. Using these guarantees requires validated logging, a credible selection range, and a regret tolerance in cost units. Information acquisition must distinguish tighter assurance from operating savings.

entries.title: Residual Reinforcement Learning for Visual Servo Control with Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Transfer
entries.abstract: We address tracking a moving object on a conveyor with a Franka Emika Panda robot arm, despite an imprecise digital twin, measurement errors, and noise. Our novel approach augments a loop-shaped inverse-Jacobian PI controller with a residual policy learned via Soft Actor-Critic in the digital twin. A delay-compensated Kalman filter fuses out-of-sequence camera measurements to provide latency-aware moving target position estimates. We compare the achieved performance to a performance bound for a class of model-based controllers derived from a frequency-domain sensitivity analysis, quantifying the minimum achievable error imposed by uncertain kinematic model mismatch. Simulation and hardware experiments indicate that our residual policy drives tracking error below the bound. Across conveyor speeds (27.9-41.8 mm/s), our method reduces mean tracking errors from 1.1-1.4 mm (baseline inverse-Jacobian PI) to 0.3-0.7 mm. These results show that learning residual corrections in a limited-fidelity simulator, combined with delay compensation, can substantially improve model-based control under modeling and measurement uncertainties while maintaining reliable sim-to-real transfer.
entries.comment: This manuscript is currently under review in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L)

entries.title: Distributed Shaping of Robot Swarms Through Spatial Moments of Arbitrary Order
entries.abstract: This paper shapes a swarm into a target pattern, such as a figure taken from an image, by controlling its spatial moments. The image is sampled into a reference configuration whose centroid and covariance set the position and principal spreads of the formation, while its higher-order moments, expressed in covariance-normalized (whitened) coordinates, encode the remaining shape. In contrast with geometric formation control, which prescribes distances, bearings, or relative positions between specific agents, this specification concerns the swarm as a whole and assigns no agent to a particular place. The key mechanism is orthogonalization in the swarm's own empirical inner product: projecting negative-gradient velocities onto the complement of low-degree polynomials sampled at the agents makes every higher-order correction preserve all lower-order moments exactly. The resulting hierarchical controller has lower triangular error dynamics and converges locally exponentially for any positive gains, so orders can be added without undoing those already achieved. A joint alternative regulates the higher moments together through a regularized Gauss–Newton step while preserving the centroid and covariance dynamics. We give bounds on the number of agents and sufficient conditions for regularity. Both controllers admit a distributed implementation that uses only relative positions and neighbor communication and retains local exponential convergence when estimation is sufficiently fast. In a distributed simulation on a sparse graph, 350 agents form an airplane from an unstructured swarm through moments up to order ten; the hierarchy reaches the full specification, while the joint law approaches it with smaller velocities.

entries.title: Exploration as Feedback in Model Predictive Path Integral Control
entries.abstract: This paper investigates how exploration affects closed-loop stability in model predictive path integral (MPPI) control. With a warm start, MPPI optimizes a control sequence by sampling candidates around the previous solution, and their covariance, the exploration covariance, is typically tuned to balance solution quality and computational cost. Small exploration is attractive because most samples then contribute to the solution, and existing stability analyses treat reduced exploration only as a bias toward the previous solution. Whether insufficient exploration can destabilize the closed loop has therefore remained open. We show that, for linear quadratic (LQ) problems with infinitely many samples, the exploration covariance also determines the feedback gain, i.e., how strongly MPPI updates the previous solution in response to the current state. With small exploration at a fixed temperature, MPPI nearly repeats the previous solution and fails to stabilize an exponentially unstable plant. Because a single covariance governs both exploration and feedback, stability and sample efficiency are in structural conflict: stabilization requires large exploration, which leaves few samples that contribute to the solution. To resolve this conflict, we propose Stabilizing Subspace MPPI (SS-MPPI), which computes the control inputs required for stabilization and samples only the rest. For LQ problems, SS-MPPI remains stable with small exploration and is thus sample-efficient. Simulations of an inverted pendulum and a quadruped robot confirm the analysis, showing that MPPI fails under small exploration, whereas SS-MPPI remains stable even with few samples.
entries.comment: 20 pages, 3 figures. Submitted to the 9th Annual Conference on Learning for Dynamics and Control (L4DC 2027)

entries.title: Integrated Co-design Framework for High-Efficiency Assembly and Integration of Small Satellites
entries.abstract: The rapid growth of small-satellite constellations has increased the need for higher manufacturing throughput, lower production costs, and shorter turnaround times. This makes efficient assembly, integration, and testing (AIT) increasingly important. Building on our prior work, this paper presents an integrated design-for-AIT approach for the 65 kg Lumelite-5 satellite. The integrated approach incorporates co-designing the satellite configuration, structural interfaces, subsystem placement, harness routing, and ground support equipment to facilitate efficient AIT. Service interfaces are centralized on one satellite side to simplify electrical ground support equipment access and routing. Skeletal support interfaces are developed to retain mounted components and service interfaces when removable enclosures are opened to expose internal harness-routing paths for inspection, troubleshooting, and rework. Defined mechanical references further support controlled removal and reinstallation of sensors and components. A removable double hinge ground-support mechanism allows the top deck to open up to 180 degrees relative to the bottom deck while accommodating interconnecting-harness articulation, without introducing permanent hinge mass and complexity to the satellite. Finally, dedicated harness-routing and tie-down provisions provide predefined yet adjustable restraint locations to accommodate as built routing variations and maintain controlled harness articulation during top-deck rotation. Through this work, we demonstrate how co-designing satellite architecture and AIT processes from the early development stages can support more scalable, repeatable, and efficient constellation production.
entries.comment: To be published in IEEE Aerospace Conference, Big Sky, MT, USA, 6-12 March, 2026

entries.title: Temporal Attention-Enhanced Mixture-of-Experts Guidance for Multi-Revolution Low-Thrust Rendezvous
entries.abstract: Multi-revolution low-thrust rendezvous requires both long-duration orbital transfer and precise terminal control. This paper proposes a temporal attention-enhanced mixture-of-experts guidance law trained by deep reinforcement learning. A far-range expert acts on modified equinoctial elements, a terminal expert acts on the relative state in the target's local frame, and a learned gate blends their thrust commands. The terminal expert encodes its observation history with a Transformer to address partial observability, and the gate uses a separate encoder to account for the resulting history-dependent command. The experts are pretrained separately, the gate is trained with both experts frozen, and the complete guidance law is then fine-tuned end to end. On 600 test missions, it achieves rendezvous in every case at tolerances of 10 m and 1 m/s, reduces mean flight time and delta-v by 50.6% and 44.5% relative to distance-based hard switching, and remains successful without retraining under navigation errors, unmodeled orbital perturbations, eclipse-induced thrust outages, and thrust loss.
entries.comment: 27 pages, 11 figures. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems

entries.title: Site-Specific Cell Shaping: An Agentic Framework
entries.abstract: An agentic framework is proposed for cell shaping in future sixth-generation (6G) wireless network planning. Cell shaping controls the coverage and interferences of base stations (BSs) through antenna parameters configuration, providing an important means of improving coverage. In contrast to conventional approaches that reply on costly performance evaluations, the proposed framework achieves intelligent and efficient antenna configuration through a perception-reasoning-reflection loop. Specifically, a Configuration Agent combines scene information, evaluation history, and reflection feedback to generate antenna configuration proposals. Then, a ray tracing(RT)-based evaluator assesses these proposals and returns a structured performance summary. Next, a Reflection Agent interprets these results to diagnose site-specific performance deficiencies, recommend feasible configuration adjustments, and accumulate conditional experience. Through this iterative process, the framework accumulates site-specific experience and progressively refines antenna configurations without human-in-the-loop intervention. Simulations in real-world urban scenarios demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves lower outage probabilities than the considered benchmark methods, highlighting the effectiveness of agentic reasoning and reflection in translating site-specific performance feedback and accumulated experience into adaptive antenna configuration decisions.

entries.title: Generalization Testing of Grid Foundation Models for Power Flow and Optimal Power Flow
entries.abstract: There is growing interest in foundation models (FMs) for power grids, particularly for power flow and optimal power flow. Their usefulness depends on generalization accuracy, which existing works test on their own benchmarks. We propose a three-axis framework to test their generalization limits: changed admittance matrices of training grids, load levels, and unseen grids. We test GENCO, LUMINA and GridSFM against the DC baseline, alongside their reported limitations, and discuss theoretical reasons for their failures. Experiments reveal that adding a line degrades all FMs more than removing one, and longer lines eventually make LUMINA and fine-tuned GENCO worse than DC. All three degrade beyond their training load range, where the loading-voltage curve steepens. On unseen grids, LUMINA degrades sharply even inside its training range, and GridSFM fails on the grid farthest from it. Thus, beyond training conditions, FMs behave more like meta-models requiring test-time fine-tuning data and compute.

entries.title: A Unified Control Framework, Mathematical Model, and Five-layer Closed-loop Case Study for Embodied Intelligence Control Systems
entries.abstract: Embodied intelligence holds that an agent develops cognition and behavior through real-time body-environment interaction, so its control system must tightly couple perception, decision making, learning, optimization, constraints, and physical execution. This report asks whether a unified framework exists, how its mathematical models unify, and how the framework is realized computably. Four conclusions emerge. (1) No single framework is accepted, but the field converges on a common skeleton: from operational-space and whole-body control to MPC, reinforcement learning, active inference, and diffusion/flow policies, all reduce to constrained sequential decision making on the configuration manifold. (2) Two languages describe it-deterministic optimal control (Euler-Lagrange plus constrained OCP, reduced in real time to a QP) and probabilistic inference (MDP/POMDP plus free-energy minimization)-rigorously bridged by control as inference and KL/path-integral control. (3) Engineering unification is already achieved by constrained optimization; the new frontier is cross-morphology, cross-task shared representation. (4) The hardest gap is provable stability and safety, the entry point for spectral, geometric, differentiable-optimization, and safe-learning methods. A single-link manipulator then runs through all five layers: L4 parses the instruction into a reference, L3 identifies a Koopman lifted linear world model, L2 solves a receding constrained QP, L1 adds torque saturation and a CBF, and L0 is the true nonlinear plant. Closed-loop tracking RMSE is 0.0218 rad with all constraints satisfied and a world-model error near 5 x 10^-6 rad, reported with curves and a 3D animation.

entries.title: Mean-field Token Steering
entries.abstract: We consider stochastic token steering through a deep stack of transformer layers as a mean-field control problem for an interacting particle system on the unit sphere, where interactions arise from the attention mechanism. In the mean-field limit, the token population evolves via a controlled integro-partial differential equation where the feedback control acts as a corrective vector field guiding the population toward an aggregate configuration of tokens in the representation space. We deduce the minimum effort control to accomplish this task over a fixed time horizon interpreted as normalized layer depth. We show that the resulting controlled dynamics for the token population can be understood as a mean-field Schrödinger bridge adapted to the sphere geometry. Building on this, we propose a novel generalization of the dynamic Sinkhorn recursion to compute the consistent token evolution. Numerical experiments confirm that the proposed approach achieves exact steering of the token population.

entries.title: HDR-DTCP: High-Dynamic-Range Differential Tissue-Coupled Wireless Powering for Tunable Biphasic Stimulation in Injectable Implants
entries.abstract: Next-generation implantable neurostimulators require efficient wireless power delivery in smaller, less invasive form factors, yet variations in tissue coupling, implantation conditions, and stimulation loads can alter received power (or requirements) and degrade energy-harvesting performance. This work presents high-dynamic-range (HDR) differential tissue-coupled powering (DTCP), termed HDR-DTCP, a body-coupled architecture in which noninvasive differential electrodes establish an AC electric field in tissue and a thread-like implant extracts power from the longitudinal potential gradient for on-chip harvesting and stimulation. Distributed coupling along the implant length, rather than receiver cross-section, enables minimally invasive injectable geometries, with harvested power scaling with implant length. A 65-nm complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) prototype integrates a reconfigurable four-stage energy harvester with automatic stage selection and a tunable constant-current biphasic stimulator, achieving 63.5% peak power-conversion efficiency (PCE) at -16.3 dBm and >50% PCE over a 9-dB input-power range. Preliminary in-vivo validation of DTCP was done with a second application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) on an injectable flexible substrate, capable of being delivered through a 14-gauge needle adjacent to the sciatic nerve of Sprague-Dawley rats (n=4). External copper-pad DTCP powering evoked repeatable hind-limb twitches and electromyography (EMG) response; ultrasound confirmed sub-millimeter nerve proximity, video-based paw-tip tracking captured the response, and 8-day post-implant dissection verified placement along the sciatic-nerve trajectory. Overall, this work provides an integrated wireless powering, energy-harvesting, and stimulation platform toward fully battery-free injectable neuromodulation implants.

entries.title: The Race between Protection and Control: Fast Reactive Reserves Against Overvoltage Cascade
entries.abstract: In an overvoltage cascade, each relay trip removes reactive power absorption and raises the voltage at other plants, often faster than controls can act. This paper determines how much fast reactive power to hold, where, and how fast, so that no contingency trips a plant. A trip certificate allows a relay to pick up if it resets before its delay expires, making the sizing a linear program. A necessary condition identifies the relays that only preventive action can protect, and the reserve of one control decreases with the relay delay and increases with its latency. In nonlinear simulations of four systems, the corrective actions prevent every trip within the analysis window for relays without reset hysteresis, and each plant's own set point is the most effective reserve. A 2% hysteresis or a small error in the relay voltage can change the reserve as much as the relay delay.

entries.title: AI Inference-Aware Optimal Power Flow: Converting Token Requirements into Grid Flexibility
entries.abstract: The rapid growth, temporal variability, and geographic concentration of electricity demand from artificial intelligence (AI) inference can aggravate transmission congestion near data centers (DCs). The spatial and temporal flexibility of inference workloads offers an opportunity to alleviate this congestion: requests can be routed across DCs or deferred within users' quality-of-service (QoS) requirements. However, inference routing primarily considers graphics processing unit (GPU) availability, leaving this flexibility underused in grid operation. Using GPU measurements, this paper models inference latency and DC power consumption to quantify the flexibility available under users' time-to-first-token (TTFT) and inter-token latency (ITL) requirements. These models are then incorporated into an AI inference-aware optimal power flow (OPF) that coordinates inference routing and power system operation among DC operators, the transmission system operator, and inference users. By linking user requests, token generation at DCs, and electricity delivery through the transmission network, the formulation schedules inference workloads subject to both users' QoS requirements and transmission constraints. Simulations on the PJM system show that, compared with computing-based routing and with electricity price-based routing, coordinating inference routing with network operation enables growing DC electricity demand deliverable to be met at lower cost.

entries.title: ANCHOR: A Port-Hamiltonian Model for Forecasting Team Dynamics in Human-in-the-Loop Systems
entries.abstract: Cyber-physical-human systems close a loop around people by sensing human behavior, predict it and act on it. Human teams are a natural target, because collaboration breaks down in ways that a timely prompt could prevent. Collaborative mixed reality makes this loop practical, since each headset senses who speaks, where its wearer looks and who stands together, and it can deliver a light prompt. In this loop, the headsets are sensors, the prompts are actuators and the team is the plant. Closing the loop needs a plant model that is small enough to learn from few teams, safe to iterate and readable by a designer. We propose ANCHOR, which models a team as a ball in an energy bowl. The bottom of the bowl is where the team rests, and it is set by the team's recent behavior, its own history and other teams. Formally, ANCHOR is a switched port-Hamiltonian system with 52 parameters, and each part stands for a testable claim from team psychology. Because of this structure, for any fitted parameters, a forecast moves away from rest only when task progress or a prompt pushes it, and prompts of bounded size that are spaced in time move it a bounded distance. On four-person teams held out from training, a team that drifts from its usual behavior returns most of the way within half a minute. After 32 s, about 24% of the deviation remains, and ANCHOR predicted 30%. Forecasts are clearly better when the resting point blends its three sources than when it uses one. ANCHOR matches the accuracy of a black-box baseline with about 40,000 parameters. It anticipates conversation collapse with an AUROC of 0.85. In simulation under assumed prompt effects, it removes 2.2 times as much breakdown time per prompt as periodic prompting.

entries.title: Reliable Conditioned Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability via Subsolution Learning on Exact Local Windows
entries.abstract: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability computes the maximal safe set and a safety filter for a given obstacle configuration, but it must be re-solved whenever the obstacles change, which a deployed robot cannot afford. Learning a single value function conditioned on the obstacle set removes the re-solve, yet it sharpens the central weakness of learned reachability: one network must now cover a whole family of safety problems, and its approximation error carries no preferred sign, so rare obstacle configurations silently produce false-safe states. To address these challenges, we present a conditioned reachability model designed so that the remaining error falls on the conservative side. Specifically, our method caps the obstacle margin, which makes the value function provably local, in the sense that obstacles farther than a known threshold cannot affect it, so the model reads only a body-frame window, trains on small scenes, and transfers to scenes of any size with millisecond per-scene preparation. Moreover, the output structure builds the value bound into the model. By training with counterexample mining over the finite-dimensional window configuration space, we maximize the claimed safe volume subject to the HJ inequality, so the learned set grows toward the true safe set from the conservative side. Across all tested obstacle settings, ours is the only method that combines recovery comparable to per-scene DeepReach training with near-zero rollout collisions. We also extend the method to a 10D quadrotor, again with markedly lower collision rates than the baselines.

entries.title: Job-Level Workload Allocation for Data Centers Under Flexible Interconnections
entries.abstract: Flexible interconnections allow data centers to connect to the grid sooner without upgrading the grid infrastructure, if they accept limits on their grid power during periods of grid stress. When a limit is reached, the data center must slow some of its computing jobs. This choice sets the cost of flexibility, because the work done by a job is worth far more than the energy it uses. This paper models how jobs respond when their power is reduced, and proposes a real-time method that shares the available power among jobs according to their value. It also gives grid planners a simple measure of how much power a data center can reduce, and for how long. A one-year case study of a 100-MW data center shows that the proposed method lowers the cost of meeting grid limits, and that on-site generation and storage lower it further.

entries.title: Certify, Then Select: Viability-Aware Runtime Steering of Frozen Diffusion Policies
entries.abstract: Diffusion policies, which generate short action sequences by denoising random noise, are a leading way to learn robot skills from demonstrations. Once deployed, they meet constraints the demonstrations never contained, and retraining for each is impractical. A safety filter edits the policy's action to satisfy them, but the edit ignores the task, and a large edit can leave the policy where it cannot continue. We propose CAST (Certified Action Selection at Test time): draw a few action chunks from the frozen policy, certify each with a barrier condition, and execute the certified chunk that a learned value ensemble ranks highest. We prove that a certified step is safe whatever the critic does; that, whenever a certified sample exists, the executed chunk stays within log N nats of the policy conditioned on feasibility, while a safety-filter projection can be singular to it; and that an exact closed-loop identity splits the gain of ranking into availability, spread and the critic's target. Certifying the next chunk is not enough: a generative controller can have safe actions available now and none later. We characterise the safe control authority of a frozen policy under finite sampling, and CAST-V preserves it through a policy-conditioned viability, estimated with a model under a finite-sample guarantee or learned from the controller's own logs (CAST-VL). On robomimic manipulation, a planar quadrotor, a MuJoCo humanoid and a unicycle, with frozen policies, CAST raises joint task-and-constraint success above the output filter in nearly every setting; certifying before ranking is decisive where a filter's edit is large, and viability removes most dead ends that one-step certification cannot see. Project page: https://clmoro.github.io/cast.

entries.title: Model-Free UPS Control Tuning for Improved Low-Voltage Ride-Through in AI Data Centers
entries.abstract: Voltage sags can trigger protection trips in uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems, abruptly reducing the power that AI data centers draw from the grid. This paper improves the low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) capability of AI data centers equipped with double-conversion UPS systems by tuning their existing converter controls. We formulate a bound-constrained optimization problem to maximize the ride-through area, defined as the integral of ride-through time over a range of retained grid voltages. To solve this problem, we develop a batched projected zeroth-order optimization algorithm with adaptive moment estimation (BPZO-Adam). The algorithm evaluates candidate control settings using only simulated ride-through times, making it suitable for vendor-supplied black-box models. Simulations using the TAMU-ERCOT electromagnetic transient (EMT) AI data center model show that tuning converter control parameters increases the ride-through area by 10.6%. In a separate study, tuning the controls yields a larger ride-through area than increasing the DC-link capacitance tenfold.

entries.title: Distance-Certified Safe Control in Unknown Environments via Spatio-Temporal Composition of Gaussian Processes
entries.abstract: In this paper, we propose a distance-certified safety control framework for unknown and dynamic environments. The proposed strategy relies on a spatio-temporal composition of Gaussian Process (GP) barriers from environment point clouds. A point-cloud-dependent covariance kernel is constructed to smoothly combine individual GP representations, yielding a continuously differentiable posterior mean and a diagonal observation Gram matrix that avoids dense covariance inversions. We then derive a closed-form calibration of the GP length scale accounting for spatial approximation errors and finite point-cloud coverage, guaranteeing a prescribed minimum distance from the true obstacle boundary. To handle moving obstacles and updated observations, the scan-based barriers are certified over finite validity horizons and smoothly combined into a time-varying Control Barrier Function (CBF). Under problem feasibility conditions, the associated CBF-based safety control guarantees forward invariance of the certified safe set, thereby ensuring the prescribed distance from the obstacles. Unicycle simulations with static and moving obstacles illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

entries.title: Lie Group Structure of Six-Degree-of-Freedom Rigid-Body Uncertainty Representation and Propagation
entries.abstract: For six-degree-of-freedom rigid-body motion, the choice of Lie-group structure affects both how well the group-theoretic mean and covariance represent the state distribution and how accurately these moments are propagated. A quaternion-based, left-trivialized semidirect-product formulation of the velocity phase space is developed for the actuated body-frame dynamics, with closed-form group operations and Jacobians that avoid matrix-group embeddings. We derive the controlled stochastic dynamics and establish that the direct- and semidirect-product formulations describe the same physical process under the specified noise model. Since the semidirect exponential coordinates account for frame changes between body twists at different poses, they capture pose–twist coupling more naturally. A lunar powered-descent experiment assesses low-order moment representations of uncertainty and propagation performance under the proposed group structure using two distinct algorithms. Compared with direct-product formulations and a linearized baseline, the proposed structure improves the representation of the banana-shaped body-velocity distribution using group-theoretic moments, yields more consistent propagated moments, and produces distribution approximations that agree more closely with the Monte Carlo reference. In this experiment, changing the group structure accounts for most of the observed improvement, highlighting the practical value of the proposed semidirect-product formulation.

entries.title: AGI: Agility Index for Power Systems Dynamic Performance, Inspired by Reynolds Number
entries.abstract: Multiple established metrics and indices exist to quantify the dynamic performance of power systems. With the growth of inverter based resources, these mostly conventional metrics and indices may not encompass all important elements and variables that hold information about the grid performance, especially the damping properties. This paper proposes the Agility Index (AGI), which is a Reynolds number-inspired metric for power system dynamics relating the ratio of inertia to damping. With the current trends towards high-power inverter assets and reduced-inertia grids, explicit attention is necessary in monitoring inertia and damping together. This paper shares insights the AGI presents about the dynamic performance of power systems.

entries.title: Bayesian Learning of Uncertain Linear System Behaviours
entries.abstract: We present a Bayesian approach to learning uncertain behavioural representations of linear dynamical systems from noisy input-output data. In behavioural systems theory, the finite-horizon behaviour of a linear system is represented by a subspace. We quantify uncertainty in this subspace through probability distributions on the Grassmann manifold. This leads to a geometric formulation of Bayesian inference over the Grassmannian. We derive the posterior distribution under Gaussian measurement noise and discuss how uncertainty in the inferred behaviour can be propagated to trajectory predictions, with a view towards data-driven control.

entries.title: Coordinating Distributed AI Servers with Industrial Loads to Reduce Grid-Interconnection Needs
entries.abstract: We show that co-locating distributed AI servers with industrial demand and coordinating AI workloads with production loads can substantially reduce the additional grid interconnection that AI computing requires. Grid interconnection is increasingly constraining the expansion of large AI data centers. Factories already have grid connections sized for their peak production loads, and we propose hosting AI servers during production valleys. We formulate a joint optimization that sizes CPU and GPU servers, schedules deadline-constrained tasks, and routes tasks among factories, and use it to compare three factory-site architectures with new large data centers serving the same demand. Applying this framework to 31 Chinese manufacturing industries, we find that AI demand and production loads often do not peak together. As a result, AI servers placed at factories and scheduled according to production peaks need about 60% less additional interconnection capacity than new large data centers, and 98% less when tasks are routed among a group's factories.

entries.title: Optimal Operating-Point Selection for Single-Linearization Trajectory Planning of Nonlinear Robot Manipulators
entries.abstract: Single-point linearization provides a computationally efficient basis for optimization-based trajectory planning of nonlinear robot manipulators. However, planning performance depends on the selected linearization point. This paper presents an offline performance-driven approach that treats the location of a single linearization as an optimization variable. Candidate operating points are sampled from a common cubic seed trajectory, and each corresponding affine model is used to solve an identical constrained finite-horizon quadratic program (QP). The resulting control sequences are executed on the original nonlinear dynamics, and the operating point minimizing the nonlinear trajectory objective is selected through grid search and bounded refinement. Evaluation on four point-to-point motions of a three-degree-of-freedom UR5 manipulator yields optimal normalized operating-point locations between 0.325 and 0.935, demonstrating trajectory-dependent selection. Compared with the best-performing conventional initial, midpoint, or terminal linearization, the proposed approach reduces the nonlinear trajectory objective by 17-18%, 21-22%, 37-38%, and 7-8% across the four tasks, respectively. Additional nonlinear execution with identical PID feedback correction confirms that the performance advantage persists for a representative task. These results demonstrate that systematic operating-point selection can substantially improve single-linearization trajectory planning while preserving a fixed affine planning model.
entries.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures. Accepted for presentation at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Advances in Computing (IEEE ICAC 2026)

entries.title: Dependable Voice Command for Multi-UAV Swarms Using Small Language Models
entries.abstract: Supervisory control of multiple autonomous unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) imposes high visual and cognitive demands on human operators, particularly when communicating mission objectives and system constraints. Voice command provides a natural interaction modality that can reduce operator workload; however, its reliability is affected by environmental noise, speech variability, and recognition errors. This paper presents a dependable voice command framework for multi-UAV swarm supervision using Small Language Models (SLMs). The proposed architecture integrates an Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) module with an SLM-based semantic processing layer to transform spoken operator commands into structured task definitions for downstream multi-UAV planning and execution. To evaluate robustness, an end-to-end assessment pipeline is developed using a Probabilistic Context-Free Grammar (PCFG) to generate synthetic supervisory commands, which are converted into audio samples with varying operator accents and environmental signal-to-noise ratios (SNR). The resulting speech signals are processed by the ASR module, and the SLM performs contextual interpretation and phonetic correction of transcriptions when required. The evaluation isolates the resilience of the voice command pipeline under acoustic degradation and speech variation, demonstrating reliable task generation for multi-UAV supervision in challenging operational conditions.

entries.title: Learn Locally, Extend Globally: Koopman Eigenfunctions and the Basin of Attraction
entries.abstract: Koopman eigenfunctions associated with the Jacobian eigenvalues of a stable equilibrium are Lyapunov functions defined exactly on its basin of attraction. We turn this into a computational procedure for power systems. Eigenfunctions estimated by extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) are written as functions of the state, made to vanish at the equilibrium by centering the lifted variable cosδ, and verified on a grid with the model: two Lyapunov candidates from the EDMD spectrum certify up to 66% of the basin of a single-machine infinite-bus system from data in the linear region. The Koopman semigroup property then extends the EDMD-Lie eigenfunction to the whole basin, recovered at the grid resolution with its isostables and isochrons.

entries.title: Technical Report of Auriga's 1:10 Scale Autonomous Vehicle Robot
entries.abstract: This report presents the design and implementation of Auriga Robotics' 1:10 scale autonomous vehicle, developed at Shahid Beheshti University's Robotics and Intelligent Automation Laboratory. The platform integrates a custom mechanical chassis, a distributed embedded system based on ESP32 microcontrollers, and a Jetson Orin NX module for high-level perception and control. The embedded layer manages sensor interfacing, real-time data acquisition, and actuator control, while the Jetson handles environment perception through deep-learning–based lane, sign, and traffic light detection, as well as decision-making and trajectory control. System communication is achieved via structured UART links, ensuring synchronized operation between perception and control subsystems. The vehicle's software stack incorporates ROS, modular firmware design, and multiple control algorithms—Stanley, PID, and Pure Pursuit—to achieve stable autonomous navigation in structured driving scenarios. The overall system demonstrates robust performance and reliability in urban-like environments, serving as a modular research platform for future autonomous driving studies.

entries.title: Impact of Grid-Forming Inverter Placement and Penetration on Local and Aggregate Frequency
entries.abstract: Modern power systems are undergoing a huge shift in generation mix, including inverter-based resources that are fundamentally changing the stability dynamics of the grid. Thus, synchronous Generators (SG) are gradually being displaced by Grid-forming inverters (GFM) that are proposed as a solution to continue supporting grid stability. However, the effect of GFM placement in the network on frequency performance and how well aggregate-frequency assessment captures placement sensitivity observed in local frequency metrics remains unclear. This paper evaluates all SG and droop-controlled GFM assignments in the IEEE 39-bus system. A reduced-order model is used for the exhaustive search with load disturbances applied separately at every eligible load bus while considering nadir and Rate of Change of Frequency (RoCoF) derived from both device rating weighted aggregate frequency and local bus frequencies. Results reveal that at fixed GFM penetration, placement produced up to 104 mHz variation in worst-case local nadir and 0.21 Hz/s in maximum local RoCoF. Aggregate-frequency assessment reduced the apparent across placements by 89% for nadir and 88% for RoCoF at 50% GFM penetration. These results indicate that aggregate-frequency assessment alone may obscure favorable or adverse placement effects on local frequency performance.
